meta.title: One control plane, three agents, twelve proofs: scenario by scenario
meta.question: Change the control plane, never the agents, and read the effect from the systems of record. For every scenario: what went in, what came out, where a property was qualified or broke, and where each number came from.
claim: Every scenario, its input and output.
Every central change, and what the runtime did next.

blocks.title: Every proof, grouped: core, capability, boundaries, negative control, govern the governor
blocks.sub: ✓ held · ~ qualified (held within a stated bound) · ✕ negative control (the embedded baseline: property broken by design). One mark per scenario; select a scenario on the Scenarios page for its contract, steps and lineage.

blocks.title: How a scenario's outcome is decided
blocks.text: CORE: P1 is the baseline and P2 the core proof (one central change; agent code, runtime process and request held fixed). CAPABILITY: P3–P8. BOUNDARIES: P9–P10, qualified by design. NEGATIVE CONTROL: P11. GOVERN THE GOVERNOR: P12. Held means the governed property the scenario tests held. Qualified means it held only within a stated bound: a kill switch cannot reach a partitioned runtime (P9), and drift was detected rather than prevented (P10). Negative control: the embedded baseline (P11) lost the property, which is exactly what it exists to show; it is not a failed test. Outcomes are read from each scenario's state directory, never from an agent's own account. Separately, the run's test assertions confirm every scenario behaved as expected: 15 of 15 did.
